test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If the mean and the mode of a particular data set are 36 and 63, respectively, then, using an empirical relation, find the value of the median of the same data set.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

63 = 3 × **Median** − 2 × 36

63 = 3 × **Median** − 72

3 × **Median** = 135 ⇒ **Median** = 45.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/41dd6fcfa97a7770cf9c2d6d1d095ecab72486f2d3d12fb1b5ec66f5c0bd4f9d.png] 

**Given:**

**Mean** = 36

**Mode** = 63

**Formula Used:**

**Median** = (**Mode** + 2 × **Mean**) ÷ 3

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Median** = (63 + 2 × 36) ÷ 3

⇒ **Median** = (63 + 72) ÷ 3

⇒ **Median** = 135 ÷ 3

⇒ **Median** = 45

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relation

For a **moderately skewed distribution**, the relation is approximately **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like the normal distribution), **Mean = Median = Mode**.

Skewness Property

If **Mean > Median > Mode**, the distribution is **positively skewed**. If **Mode > Median > Mean**, it is **negatively skewed**.</p
